The foundational pull request introduces a new, dedicated offloading component for vLLM v1, establishing the core infrastructure for managing and transferring Key-Value (KV) data. It sets up abstract interfaces for the scheduler to oversee offloaded data and provides concrete mechanisms for workers to perform these transfers asynchronously, laying the groundwork for more flexible memory management.

## Abstract Interfaces

The design centers on abstract manager classes: it defines an abstract OffloadingManager class intended for the scheduler, responsible for tracking offloaded data, preparing load/store operations, and managing the lifecycle of KV blocks, including lookup, touch, and eviction protection. On the worker side, it implements the OffloadingQueueManager to asynchronously manage KV data transfers.

The architecture is described further in the RFC: offloading is enabled using a new OffloadingConnector, with minimal changes to vLLM's core. On the scheduler side, this connector delegates to an abstract OffloadingManager. The OffloadingManager is responsible for bookkeeping allocation and evictions of offloaded data. Its output is encoded over KVConnectorMetadata and sent to workers.

## The `group_idx` Concept and Storage Keys

The `group_idx` you mentioned relates to the KV cache group index used in the on-disk storage layout. According to the KV Offloading Usage Guide, the directory structure uses block hashes and group indices to organize stored blocks. The layout uses the first 3 hex chars of the block hash, then the next 2 hex chars plus the KV cache group index (g<group_idx>), then the full block hash in hex as the filename; config.json records the run details such as block size and number of KV groups, and is written on first start.

Each rank writes blocks under its own _r<rank> sibling directory, so multiple ranks can safely share the same root_dir.

Regarding how storage keys are generated (relevant to `OffloadKey` / `make_offload_key`): to enable KV cache sharing between multiple vLLM instances using the same root_dir, the PYTHONHASHSEED environment variable must be set to the same fixed value on every instance. To activate KV offloading: by default the offloading size is set to None, which means no KV offloading is enabled; when set, vLLM will enable KV cache offloading to CPU using the kv_offloading_backend. The backend to use for KV cache offloading supports 'native' (vLLM native CPU offloading) and 'lmcache'; KV offloading is only activated when kv_offloading_size is set.
